findings.title: Evidence traceability accuracy: two inaccurate statements in earlier revisions
findings.detail: One Medium covering two corrections of the same kind — the accuracy of the evidence package's own traceability claims — not two separate findings. (1) Same-executor review and required backfill: the previous revision described the five-axis review as performed by the implementation author under a review waiver, and said independent Critical/High review had to be backfilled before M1 completion. That was inaccurate: the implementation author is Claude Opus 5 and the reviewer is a separate Codex executor, so the review of this change is independent, and the M1-001 through M1-003 waiver is neither invoked nor applicable to M1-PKG-002. (2) Evidence current-state claims that go stale on commit: the previous revision asserted that the four evidence files were untracked and not committed. That is a snapshot of the author working tree and becomes false the moment the reviewer creates the required evidence-only follow-up commit, which is the intended delivery path for this package.
findings.resolution: Both statements are fixed by this evidence update, in summary.md and in commands.json. (1) The same-executor and backfill wording is removed and replaced with the independent-review status recorded under authorship and reviewFindings. (2) The untracked/not-committed current-state wording is replaced with a durable description: the package is intentionally outside 3e8ccb94b0a71edd882471913994fef385f12229, it is delivered in a separate evidence-only follow-up commit created by the Codex reviewer after verification, that commit's SHA cannot be self-referenced and so is left unstamped and read from git history via evidenceUpdateCommitDiscovery, and the Claude author staged and committed nothing.

sandboxDistinction.summary: The author session ran inside a seatbelt sandbox that forbids the nested sandbox SwiftPM creates for manifest evaluation and build execution. Every affected command failed identically on unmodified HEAD, so the restriction was environmental and not caused by this change. The reviewer environment has no such restriction.
sandboxDistinction.failureSignature: error: '<package>': Invalid manifest ... then sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted, then error: fatalError. Nothing is compiled and no test is executed.
sandboxDistinction.retryRule: Each blocked command was retried with --disable-sandbox. For swift test and swift build the flag is accepted after the subcommand. For swift package it is a global option and must precede the describe subcommand: swift package --disable-sandbox --package-path <path> describe --type json. Placing it after describe fails with "Unknown option '--disable-sandbox'", exit 64.
sandboxDistinction.scopeOfFlag: --disable-sandbox only disables SwiftPM's own nested sandbox. It does not change package identity, target ownership, gate names, gate argv, or test outcomes. The gate committed to cigates.py does not contain the flag.
sandboxDistinction.unaffected: The Python tools, swift-format lint, git diff --check, and the backlog validator all ran unmodified without the flag.
